correctness.rationale: In W, (xu+yw)^2=(xy+y²)u+y²w, so the only idempotent is zero, W²=W, and the square-zero locus is exactly ku. Automorphisms preserve that line, and uw and w² successively force the coefficient of w in the image of w and the scaling of u to be 1. Thus the only freedom is w↦w+bu. Lagrange interpolation gives the moments of 1/D_i in degrees 0–3 as 0,0,1,s, so the displayed squares reproduce U²=0, UV=U/2, V²=U+V; their coefficients have distinct a_i/b_i and span the square. For any algebra in the stratum, two independent linear probes on A² give diagonal bilinear forms; choosing the first nonzero on all square vectors makes its relative operator with the second have simple spectrum because the square lines are distinct. Thus any natural basis is monomial. The unique relation among the three squares has all entries nonzero. Evaluating u²=0 shows that all coordinates of u are nonzero; normalizing them to 1 yields square coefficients summing to zero. If two normalized w-coordinates coincide, the entire image of the squaring map is contained in a line (combine the equal summands using that relation), contradicting W²=W by polarization. The Vandermonde system in 1,2t_i,t_i² has a unique solution, giving precisely the displayed squares. An isomorphism fixes the intrinsic u in square coordinates, so it can only permute the normalized basis, and it must translate the unordered w-coordinate triple. Conversely the coordinate permutation for a translating triple respects the multiplication by uniqueness of the decomposition of the square map of W. An automorphism translates a finite triple to itself, so summing gives b=0 and distinctness gives the identity. Centering removes translations, and Vieta's formulas with discriminant −4p³−27q² give exactly the indicated open plane as a set of classes, not a fine moduli scheme. Every idempotent of the ambient algebra lies in W, and its derived series stays W. Independent Vandermonde solves on four rational triples recover the square coefficients, the example and the cubic discriminants. These finite checks supplement, not replace, the exhaustion argument.

value.rationale: The fixed-square invariant selects a natural family in the setting of the survey's classification question. The value is this structural simplification and rigidity, not recataloguing known algebras.
